# Widget catalog

<!-- Generated by scripts/docs.js from each widget's schema.json. Edit the schema, then run `npm run docs`. -->

Pick widgets from this list only. Before using a widget, open its README for the exact fields and an example.

Grid sizes: S = 3, M = 6, L = 9, full = 12 columns. Each row of widgets should add up to 12.

| Widget | Use when | Don't use when | Sizes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`bar_chart`](bar_chart/README.md) | Comparing a measure across categories (revenue by rep, tickets by priority) or a short run of periods (revenue by quarter). Use horizontal bars for rankings and long names. | There is only one number (use kpi), it's a trend over more than 8 periods or has missing periods (use line_chart), it's part-to-whole (use donut), the categories are ordered process stages (use funnel), the user needs exact values for many records (use table), or there are more than 30 categories (aggregate to top N first). | M, L, full |
| [`donut`](donut/README.md) | Part-to-whole for one total split into 2 to 6 parts: revenue mix by category, open order lines by item class, Commercial vs SLED split. | The parts don't add up to a meaningful whole, or you are comparing values across categories (use bar_chart), there are more than 6 parts (group the smallest into "Other", or use bar_chart), or the split changes over time (use line_chart or a stacked bar_chart). | S, M, L |
| [`funnel`](funnel/README.md) | A process with ordered stages: a fulfillment pipeline (ordered, awaiting receipt, received, shipped, invoiced), a sales pipeline, or any flow where stage-to-stage drop-off or the count waiting at each step matters. | The categories have no natural order (use bar_chart), they are parts of one whole with no flow (use donut), or the user needs the individual orders (use table). | M, L, full |
| [`gauge`](gauge/README.md) | A single metric judged against a threshold or target: margin vs a policy floor, GP attainment vs quota, fill rate vs target, days to ship vs a maximum. | There is no threshold or target (use kpi), several values need comparing (use bar_chart), or the metric's history matters more than where it stands now (use line_chart with a reference line). | S, M |
| [`heatmap`](heatmap/README.md) | One measure cross-tabbed by two dimensions: margin by manufacturer and quarter, orders by branch and item class, revenue by rep and KPA. Missing cells stay visible as gaps. | There is only one dimension (use bar_chart), the columns are a long time series for a few rows (use line_chart), or the user needs records with mixed fields (use table). | M, L, full |
| [`kpi`](kpi/README.md) | The user wants a single headline metric at a point in time: a total, count, average, or rate (open AR, tickets this week, win rate). | The number is judged against a floor, ceiling, or goal (use gauge), several values need comparing across categories (use bar_chart), or the user needs individual records (use table). | S, M |
| [`line_chart`](line_chart/README.md) | A trend over time with more than 8 periods, or any time series with missing or withheld periods: monthly margin, weekly revenue, backorder aging over time. | The categories aren't time periods (use bar_chart), there are 8 or fewer periods and exact heights matter (use bar_chart), or there is one current number (use kpi, or gauge against a target). | M, L, full |
| [`table`](table/README.md) | The user needs to see individual records or exact values: open tickets, top deals, overdue invoices, a list of accounts. | The point is a comparison (use bar_chart), a trend (use line_chart), a cross-tab of one measure by two dimensions (use heatmap), or a single total (use kpi). Don't dump raw data: aggregate or pick the top N. | M, L, full |
